subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm aiming for an efficient but rich module, around 400 lines, designing an armoured 6-wheel hauler truck with a cab, sealed cargo pod with glowing seals, roof turret, and neon trim, built using the SDK's builder and joint system to keep the wheel chassis simple.

I'm sketching dimensions and part placement: cab at the front, pod at the rear, three wheel axles, chassis height, and planning custom paints and SVG textures for hazard stripes, decals, screens, and a glowing neon emblem, using plane geometry parts for the visual details.

Still building the cab and hood...

Now I'm detailing the pod: ring bands, end caps, cradle brackets, glowing seal strips, hex emblem decals, warning stripes, and clamp latches on both sides, checking the pod's radius and position fit the truck bed dimensions. I'm also planning the roof turret with yaw/pitch joints and a glowing-lens gun barrel, plus an antenna, light bar, and exhaust stacks behind the cab.

Now I'm working out the six wheels, each with a tire cylinder, rim, hub, lug nuts, tread blocks, and a glowing neon hub ring, mounted via spin joints with fenders covering them, mirrored across both sides of the truck.

I'm also adding a magenta underglow box beneath the chassis and detail pipes/cables using swept curves, while double-checking the tread block radius and height so they sit flush against the tire surface without sinking below ground level.

Now I'm settling on a color palette (hull paint, dark trim, plate, magenta/cyan/amber accents, hazard stripe) and planning SVG textures for hazard stripes and a hexagonal cyan emblem with a padlock motif.

Working through the geometry of placing decal planes on the pod's cylindrical surface — checking offsets so the plane doesn't float too far off the curved surface — and realizing it's simpler to just use the engine's built-in decal function targeting the pod part directly rather than manually positioning a plane.

I'll use decal projection for the "SEALED" emblem and door numbers too, applying it to flat box surfaces where it works cleanly, plus add a small glowing cyan box behind the cab glass for a dash-light effect. Writing helper functions for boxes...

Now I'm defining the wheel hinge joints and turret yaw/pitch joints with their parent chain, skipping the rear hatch door since it'll stay static. I'll add stairs with handrails along the pod and side cargo toolboxes instead of fuel tanks, plus a sweeping glowing cable running from the cab rear to the pod front using a catmull curve.

Writing sweep options...
